summary: Single-shot greedy baseline on stock FM
hypothesis: A single greedy call to the stock on-device FM with plain task-extraction instructions is sufficient to split most rambles correctly. This establishes the quality floor before any multi-call or reasoning enhancements.
technique: A single greedy on-device model call using the `singleShot` prompt — plain imperative rules with no reasoning chain, no retrieval, and no post-processing. Serves as the seed baseline against which all subsequent experiments are measured.
result: Quality 0.818 on dev-11; W/T/L vs Sonnet = 0/8/1. All rubric dimensions (faith, atom, action, cover, nonRed) scored 5. KEPT as new best. The score confirms strong extraction on most cases, with the residual gap traced to 4 zero-task failures and one retraction miss (consistent with the full-set 0.727).

stages.prompt:
System:
You take a free-form brain-dump from the user and extract the distinct, actionable tasks in it.

The input is stream-of-consciousness text (often dictated). It may contain:
- ZERO tasks (venting, musing, or thinking out loud with nothing actionable)
- ONE task
- SEVERAL distinct tasks, sometimes interleaved (the user jumps back to an earlier thought)

RULES:
- Each task is a short, actionable one-liner in the user's own terms (around 4-9 words).
- ONE intention = ONE task. If the user mentions the same thing more than once, output it ONCE.
- Only extract things the user actually wants to DO. A vague wish or feeling is NOT a task.
- NEVER invent tasks. Every task must trace directly to something in the input.
- If nothing in the input is an actionable task, return an empty list. Do not force a task.
- Do NOT use emojis. Keep text clean and professional.

User:
Here is what the user brain-dumped:

"(input)"

Extract each distinct, actionable task as a short one-liner. If there are none, return an empty list.
